newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta loses ground vs mark, all eyes on auction.
newsitem.headline: Peseta loses ground vs mark, all eyes on auction.

text.p: The peseta eased versus the mark in late Wednesday trade in a small wave of profit-taking before Thursday's Bank of Spain repurchase auction, traders said.
By 1700 GMT, the peseta was at 83.65/68 compared with late Tuesday's levels of 83.56/59.
"It's simply a technical adjustment, a correction in response to the recent strong rise of the peseta," a trader said.
Traders said the Bank of Spain's regular repurchase auction on Thursday was now absorbing the market's interest.
"Tomorrow is an important day because now that we've had December CPI, the Bank of Spain may be in a position to adjust rates at the auction," said one trader.
Spain's December CPI came in roughly in line with expectations, rising 0.3 percent month-on-month to give a yearly gain of 3.2 percent.

Traders warned that if the central bank declined to trim its key money market rate, which currently stands at 6.25 percent, the peseta could make a move toward the 83.35/40 barrier and on toward 83.00 per mark.
A Reuter poll showed that eight out of 10 economists expected no rate change.
